summary: R. T. Vyas was an Indologist. He served as General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara from 1993 to 1994.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held positions at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, ICPR, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

R. Venkatraman is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and served there as Reader (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) worked in philosophy and other fields. He attended St. Xavier's Collegiate School (~1875–1876) and University College London (~1878–1880), and founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. Around 2013, she served as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and was appointed Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

Radha Burnier (1923–2013) worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Kalakshetra and Banaras Hindu University, and served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre from approximately 1954 to 1980.

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) was an Indian historian and Indologist. Educated at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University, he held posts at Patna University, Ganesh Dutt College, Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University.

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indology and history scholar educated at the University of Calcutta (~1901–1905). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917), Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1917–1921), and the University of Mysore (~1917–1921).

Radhika Herzberger (born 1938) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (~1974–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and served as Director of Rishi Valley School from around 1980 to 2012.

Radoslav Katičić (1930–2019) worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, University of Zagreb (~1949–1954), he held posts at the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts (~1973–2019) and the University of Vienna (~1977–1998).

Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure. He held positions at Wadham College (2012–2013) and Harvard University (attested 2015).

Rafał Jan Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. A PhD candidate at Stanford University (attested 2015), he was supervised by Paul Harrison (attested 2018) and taught by John R. McRae and Luis Oscar Gómez.
Raffaele Catà is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed his laurea at the University of Bologna (2011–2012) under supervisor Manlio Iofrida and co-supervisor Saverio Marchignoli.

Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1969–1974). He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1981–1994) and the University of Rome (~1994–2020).
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University in 1981, supervised by Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. Active in philosophy and religious studies, he taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was an Indology, Iranian, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at University of the Punjab, London, and Leiden. He founded the International Academy of Indian Culture in 1932, serving as Director in 1934, and taught at Sanatan Dharma College.

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Sir Parashurambhau College and held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, including Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department (attested 1953) and Professor.
